questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To find a place where I could learn something new and explore a different part of the world with a different worldview.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Moderately easily. The university is quite organised but some parts were really hard to figure out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. I had to do everything myself and find out information on my own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different types of housing for students. There were Halls, Residential Colleges etc. Essentially the same thing but slighty different structure and some had meal plans others didn't.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a mandatory meal plan. Food was sometimes extremely spicy and quite bland. Ate out many times to keep my sanity.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Eat out more. enjoy life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was mold in my room and the housing administration didn't care at all.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very complex and stupid with long lines waiting. multiples times for different things. Why so complicated and time wasting???

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Had to stand in a line for three hours to get a card. Then the same again the week after to the the visa.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Other students that knew more about the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. had to go though three rounds to get enough classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the registration with some friends so you dont get bored.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some where on a good level where others where unnecessarily difficult, ny jamming three courses into one and putting way too much content in little time. Not enjoyable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very strict. No amount of freedom to think and act in your own way. You have to learn the way they want or you will loose points. And their way was certainly not the most efficient at times. At UCPH we have the freedom to learn the way we learn best and to explore.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EC3322 Industrial Organisation
CS2100 Computer Organisation
ST3236 Stochastic Processes
EC3333 Financial Economics

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Industrial Organisation was really good. The professor didn't put as much pressure and he was reasonable and very nice. 

The others were kind of awful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Hospital Trip. This is extremely expensive, especially if going to private hospital. Get insurance!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food can be really cheap. Especially on campus and hawker centres. Food in supermarket is insanely expensive, especially western foods and fruits and vegetables.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of activities. Try out stuff, it is fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Scuba Diving. Golfing. Just walking around and experiencing the country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to different places in singapore and definitely visit Malaysia. Especially Tioman Island for scuba diving if you are into that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. They are all very nice and speak good English. So it is easy to get into contact with people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I arrived earlier than all the other exchangers, so I had no choice but to talk to the locals. That was very cool to experience.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The strictness. I like freedom to do whatever I want whenever I want. But they are just very strict there.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is very competitive and hard to perform well here. It is very hot outside so be prepared. You will get thousands of mosquito bites.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want a chill and relaxing exchange. Either this place is not for you or take the easy entry level course. Dont take courses for your level ie. 3000 and 4000. They are extremely difficult and time consuming.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being done with exam and going on vacation.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from family and friends and not going insane with the workload and pressure they put on students.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: While I am grateful to have been given the opportunity to go to NUS and stay in the country. I simply cannot lie and say it was the greatest experience of my life. There were of course some good moments. But the majority of the time was spent wanting it to end. There were many things in the university which just did not go well with the way I want to live. The pressure on students, is huge and multiple students committed suicide throughout just my stay. We heard news about it multiple times.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
